sourcedFrom: MC1sc™ SUB-COMPACT PISTOL / MC2c™ COMPACT PISTOL — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 105451 (2018 or later)
cleanIntro: The MC strips without a tool and without pulling the trigger, which is its best feature and the source of its one trap: the striker comes out of the BACK of the slide, and it only stays under control if the action is locked open when the cover plate leaves. Do that in the right order and the whole gun is four pieces in under a minute.

steps.title: Safety ON if it has one, and nothing on the trigger
steps.action: Set the manual safety fully to ON if your gun is fitted with one — not every MC is — keep the muzzle somewhere harmless, and keep fingers and everything else off the trigger for the whole unload.
steps.quote: Set the manual safety (if so equipped) fully to the “ON” (SAFE) position. During unloading, never allow fingers or any other object to contact the trigger.
steps.cite: MC1sc™ SUB-COMPACT PISTOL / MC2c™ COMPACT PISTOL — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 105451 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM

steps.title: Magazine out first
steps.action: Press the magazine release and take the magazine out before you touch the slide. Doing it the other way round just chambers a fresh round from a loaded magazine.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine by pressing on the magazine release
steps.cite: MC1sc™ SUB-COMPACT PISTOL / MC2c™ COMPACT PISTOL — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 105451 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM

steps.title: Slide fully back, then lock it open with the slide stop
steps.action: Grip the rear serrations, pull the slide fully rearward, and while holding it there push up on the slide stop lever with your thumb. Then ease the slide forward until it locks open. That stroke is what pulls the chambered round out.
steps.quote: While holding it rearward, apply upward pressure with your thumb to engage the slide stop lever and slowly release the slide from the rearward position until it locks in the open position
steps.cite: MC1sc™ SUB-COMPACT PISTOL / MC2c™ COMPACT PISTOL — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 105451 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM

steps.title: Chamber, magazine well and magazine — eyes and finger
steps.action: Three places, checked both ways. On a subcompact the ejection port is small and a round can sit where a glance will not find it.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine and visually and physically inspect the chamber, magazine well and magazine to be certain the firearm is unloaded before disassembling the firearm
steps.cite: MC1sc™ SUB-COMPACT PISTOL / MC2c™ COMPACT PISTOL — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 105451 — DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: Eye protection on
steps.action: Glasses before the cover plate moves. There is a striker assembly under spring load immediately behind it.
steps.quote: Wear eye protection during disassembly and cleaning.
steps.cite: MC1sc™ SUB-COMPACT PISTOL / MC2c™ COMPACT PISTOL — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 105451 — DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: ⛔ Action locked OPEN, then the slide cover plate button in and plate out
steps.action: With the action locked open, push the slide cover plate button in and slide the cover plate out of the slide. The action being open is what keeps the striker under control while the plate comes off — this is the step people do with the slide closed and then chase a striker across the bench.
steps.quote: Push in the slide cover plate button (the patent pending slide cover plate design is used under license from Strike Industries) and slide the slide cover plate out of the slide (Fig. 14).
steps.cite: MC1sc™ SUB-COMPACT PISTOL / MC2c™ COMPACT PISTOL — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 105451 — DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: Close the action gently — the gun ejects its own striker
steps.action: Grasp the rear serrations, pull the slide fully rearward and release it GENTLY. Closing pushes the striker assembly out of the back of the slide on its own. Let it go with a snap and the striker leaves under spring power instead.
steps.quote: Close the action by grasping the rear of the slide at the serrations pulling the slide fully rearward and then releasing it gently. This will allow the slide to push out the striker assembly.
steps.cite: MC1sc™ SUB-COMPACT PISTOL / MC2c™ COMPACT PISTOL — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 105451 — DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: Striker out, then the slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Take the striker assembly off, then push the slide fully forward toward the muzzle and off the frame. No tools, no trigger pull — this design does not need the trigger pressed to release the slide.
steps.quote: You can then remove the striker assembly, push the slide fully forward towards the muzzle end and slide it off the frame (Fig. 15).
steps.cite: MC1sc™ SUB-COMPACT PISTOL / MC2c™ COMPACT PISTOL — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 105451 — DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly — push muzzle-ward, then lift out
steps.action: Hold the slide, push the recoil spring assembly toward the muzzle end, then pull it up and out. Push first, lift second; lifting straight away binds it against the barrel.
steps.quote: Holding the slide in one hand, push the recoil spring assembly toward the muzzle end of the slide, pull it up and remove it from the slide
steps.cite: MC1sc™ SUB-COMPACT PISTOL / MC2c™ COMPACT PISTOL — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 105451 — DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: Barrel out by the locking cams
steps.action: Hold the barrel by its locking cams, lift, push toward the muzzle, then pull it up and out. Holding it by the cams rather than the hood is what keeps your fingers off the chamber mouth as it comes free.
steps.quote: Holding the barrel by the barrel locking cams, lift it and push it toward the muzzle end of the slide, pull it up and remove it from the slide (Fig. 17).
steps.cite: MC1sc™ SUB-COMPACT PISTOL / MC2c™ COMPACT PISTOL — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 105451 — DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: Field strip complete — four pieces and the frame
steps.action: Slide, barrel, recoil spring assembly, striker assembly, frame. Mossberg assigns anything past this to a gunsmith or the Product Service Center, and says going further voids the warranty.
steps.quote: Further disassembly should only be performed by a qualiﬁed gunsmith or the Product Service Center.
steps.cite: MC1sc™ SUB-COMPACT PISTOL / MC2c™ COMPACT PISTOL — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 105451 — DISASSEMBLY

deepAbsentReason: Mossberg publishes one teardown for the MC and stops at the field strip, assigning anything further to a qualified gunsmith or the Product Service Center and warning that going past it voids the warranty. ⛔ No deeper path is invented.

cleaning.name: RE-PROVE IT EMPTY, AND CLEAR THE BENCH
tasks: Chamber, magazine well and magazine checked again before solvent
⛔ No ammunition anywhere near the cleaning area
Eye protection through cleaning AND assembly
cleaning.quote: Always make sure that no ammunition is located in the area where you clean your firearm.
cleaning.src: MC1sc™ SUB-COMPACT PISTOL / MC2c™ COMPACT PISTOL — Mossberg owner's manual, CLEANING AND LUBRICATION

cleaning.name: BARREL, SLIDE AND STRIKER CHANNEL
tasks: Solvent through bore and chamber, patches until clean
Breech face and under the extractor with a nylon brush
Barrel locking cams and the slide's corresponding recesses
⛔ Striker channel DRY — solvent left in it is a light strike waiting to happen
cleaning.quote: Use the instructions and equipment provided in a quality firearm cleaning kit.
cleaning.src: MC1sc™ SUB-COMPACT PISTOL / MC2c™ COMPACT PISTOL — Mossberg owner's manual, CLEANING AND LUBRICATION

cleaning.name: LUBRICATE SPARINGLY — it is a carry gun
tasks: A trace on the slide rails and the barrel's bearing surfaces
Wipe the outside back to a film; a pocket gun collects lint on oil
cleaning.quote: Clean and lubricate your firearm as soon as possible after use.
cleaning.src: MC1sc™ SUB-COMPACT PISTOL / MC2c™ COMPACT PISTOL — Mossberg owner's manual, CLEANING AND LUBRICATION

reassembly: Barrel into the slide by its locking cams, seated home.
Recoil spring assembly in — down, then back toward the breech until it seats.
Slide onto the frame from the front and run it fully rearward.
Striker assembly into the back of the slide, the way it came out.
Slide cover plate on, pushed across until the button clicks up through it.
⛔ Check the cover plate is fully seated and the button is proud — it is what retains the striker.
Rack it several times, then function test.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber and magazine well checked by eye and finger. Rack the slide several times and confirm it locks open on an empty magazine and closes fully on the slide stop. If a manual safety is fitted, set it ON and pull the trigger — nothing should move — then OFF and confirm the trigger resets. ⛔ Confirm the slide cover plate is fully seated before the gun goes anywhere: it is the only thing holding the striker assembly in the slide.
